news.title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight
news.lede: World Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 England. Stanway, Le Tissier and Russo on target. England secured a 3-1 first-leg victory over Greece in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie but were unable to produce the convincing performance they would have hoped for, against a hugely unfancied Greek side. Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Ioanna Papatheodorou goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg.

news.title: Greece 1-3 England: Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo on target for Lionesses in World Cup play-off
news.lede: England are in control of their World Cup play-off with Greece after winning the first leg 3-1 in Crete. Goals from Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo moved the Lionesses into a strong position for Tuesday's second leg in Leicester - although Calliste Brookshire, who plays for Rangers in Scotland, pulled one back late on for a Greece side ranked 58th in the world. The winner will play Slovakia or Ukraine in round two on the road to Brazil 2027. Lauren James saw a stunning chip from long range ruled out for offside in the first half but the Lionesses - forced into the play-offs after finishing behind Spain in qualifying - were not at their sharpest in that period and they were almost shocked when Ioanna Papatheodorou cracked a shot against the crossbar from 35 yards.

news.title: Wexford School to represent Ireland at School World Cup in China
news.lede: The senior team at Wexford CBS are set to travel to Suzhou, China to represent Ireland at the 2026 International School Sport Federation Football World Cup. The team was invited to take part after they won the FAI Under-17 National Junior Cup in 2025. They will become the first Irish team to compete in the tournament since St Benildus College headed to Sardinia in 1999. They will leave for Shanghai on 14 October, before travelling to Suzhou for the start of the tournament on 18 October.

news.title: Morocco U-17 Women’s Team Coach Reveals World Cup Squad
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco U-17 women’s national team coach Younes Rabie has revealed the final list of players called up to represent the country at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The tournament will be hosted by Morocco from October 17 to November 8, giving the young Atlas Lionesses the opportunity to compete on home soil in a major international tournament. The squad list: Fatiha Naam Meriem Zeqaqi Chaymae Bouzrou Laila Boushaba Malak Krafia Anissa Hamdani Hiba Youssoufi Imene Diyen Charaf Boughazi Meryam Oubella Rita El Miroun Nayla Aagaou Sofia Ben Amar Sara El Hajjiouti Nora El Rhachoua Wachol Sonia Abajiou Nessma Mouradi Aya Ait Khouya Imane Dhissi Amana Lakradi The squad will now enter the final stage of preparations ahead of the competition, with the coaching staff using two closed-door friendly matches to assess the team and fine-tune its preparations.
